subject: car exhaust
title: What If You Left Your Car Idling Every Morning?

scenes.text: What if you idled your car every morning to warm it up? Your engine would rather you drove.
Most manufacturers say about 30 seconds is enough, then drive off gently, even on cold days.
Every hour of idling burns roughly a quarter to a half gallon of fuel, depending on engine size.
Ten minutes each morning adds up to about sixty hours a year, roughly fifteen to thirty gallons burned going nowhere.
Meanwhile, the catalytic converter that cleans the exhaust starts working much sooner when you drive than when you idle.
Across the US, personal car idling wastes about 3 billion gallons of fuel a year. Driving is the real warm-up.

description:
What if you left your car idling every morning? The US Department of Energy says idling burns about a quarter to a half gallon of fuel per hour, and most manufacturers recommend driving off gently after about 30 seconds.
Driving warms the engine and the catalytic converter faster than idling, and personal-vehicle idling wastes about 3 billion gallons of fuel a year in the US.
